subject: Response slab & escalation coverage — packaging and discount proposal
messages:
From: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@brightcart.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 09:14:00 -07:00
Subject: SLA options + potential volume discount

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency profile looks promising. Before we loop in procurement I need to understand how Redwood thinks about SLA packaging for a customer of our size. A few specific asks:

- Uptime tiers you offer (and the crediting methodology)
- Typical response-time windows for P1/P2 incidents and the hours those apply (business vs 24x7)
- Whether escalation coverage (oncall roster, SLA playbooks) is included or add-on
- How discounts are applied for committed monthly token volume (multi-tiered vs flat percent)

We are evaluating a 12–24 month commit and would want clear pricing bands and an example addendum we could circulate internally. Can you send a short packaging proposal and an outline of what you need from procurement to get to signature?

Appreciate it —
Paul
Paul Henderson
Director of Platform Engineering, BrightCart
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@brightcart.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jul 2025 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SLA options + potential volume discount

Paul — thanks for the clear list. I attached an initial draft that covers packaging and a pricing grid for three commit bands. High-level answers here, then Ben/Marissa have suggested tweaks on the discount math and escalation options.

Quick summary:
- Uptime tiers: 99.5% (standard), 99.9% (assured), 99.95% (enterprise). Credit bands are slabbed by incident class and monthly uptime percentage (see attached SLA_Addendum_BrightCart_v2.pdf).
- Response windows: P1: 1 hour recognition, 4 hour target full response (24x7 for enterprise; business-hours for standard). P2: 4 hour recognition, 24 hour target.
- Escalation coverage: Included for enterprise; available as an add-on retainer for standard/assured. Add-on includes named escalation path, monthly oncall hours, and quarterly tabletop review.
- Discounts: Tiered by committed monthly tokens; volume bands in spreadsheet. We can do step-downs for multi-year commits.

Next steps I propose: 1) Ben to confirm margin-friendly discount deliverable; 2) I send the SLA addendum + a short commercial term sheet for procurement; 3) Quick sync (30m) to align the playbook for escalation. Does Thursday 10am PT work?

Attachments: SLA_Addendum_BrightCart_v2.pdf, pricing_breakdown_brightcart.xlsx

Cheers,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>
To: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 10:21:00 -07:00
Subject: internal: BrightCart - discount/packaging suggestion

Jasmine / Marissa — looping in a suggested commercial approach. I kept the list simple so legal/procurement can digest quickly.

Suggested packaging (preserving Redwood pricing tiers):
- Pilot band (no commit): baseline list price, standard support
- Commit A (>= 5M tokens/mo): 12% discount, assured SLA (99.9%), optional escalation retainer at $8k/mo for 24x7 coverage (includes 40 oncall hours)
- Commit B (>= 20M tokens/mo): 20% discount, enterprise SLA (99.95%) + 24x7 escalation included with 60 oncall hours, quarterly tabletop included
- Commit C (>= 50M tokens/mo + 24 mo term): 28% discount, enterprise SLA + named SLT escalation roster, priority routing, 80 oncall hours + annual playbook review

Notes on escalation retainer: attachable to Commit A only; for Commits B/C we bake in the higher coverage. We should keep an opt-out clause if usage drops below the band for two consecutive months.

Marissa: do you see any pushback on the retainer numbers from renewals/CS? Jasmine: if you want me to soften the step between 20M and 50M I can propose an intermediate band with a reduced uplift.

Ben
VP, Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 22 Jul 2025 14:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: internal: BrightCart - discount/packaging suggestion

Ben / Jasmine — quick edits from CS/ops perspective so we don't overpromise.

- Recommend Commit B include a 30-day ramp clause where escalation coverage is scaled in (first 30 days: business-hours oncall; full 24x7 after verified traffic patterns). Helps avoid immediate ops spikes.
- For Commit C, shift the 80 oncall hours to "up to 80" and add an overage rate ($200/hr) to protect capacity.
- Add clear runbook handoffs and a mutual action plan attachment with acceptance criteria for go-live. That MPL (mutual plan) reduces ambiguity for triage.

I'll take the lead on adding the ramp language to the SLA addendum and draft the mutual action plan. Once Jasmine confirms, she can send to Paul with attachments + DocuSign link.

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Jasmine Liu <jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com>
To: Paul Henderson <paul.henderson@brightcart.com>, procurement@brightcart.com
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood-inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Wed, 23 Jul 2025 15:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Final packaging + SLA addendum (attached) — next steps

Paul — attaching the updated SLA_Addendum_BrightCart_v2.pdf (includes Marissa's ramp language) and the pricing_breakdown_brightcart.xlsx. Key points in this bundle:

- Commit bands and associated discounts (see spreadsheet, tab "bands")
- Escalation coverage mechanics: Commit A can add retainer; Commits B/C include 24x7 escalation but with a 30-day ramp on B as noted
- Overage and downgrade mechanics: usage below the band for 2 consecutive months triggers a downgrade review; overages billed monthly at published rates
- Mutual Action Plan (MAP) included in the addendum; acceptance criteria and runbook handoff checklist are explicit

If this matches your expectations we can: 1) send the DocuSign envelope (I will include the SLA addendum + term sheet), 2) have procurement/Legal review and return redlines to me (jasmine.liu@redwood-inference.com). I will aim to keep redlines minimal — Ben and Marissa are aligned on the commercial guardrails.

DocuSign preview: https://docusign.com/preview/BRG-4392
HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/BRG-4392

Would Thursday 10am PT still work for the short sync?

Thanks — looking forward to moving this along.

Attachments (stubs): SLA_Addendum_BrightCart_v2.pdf (PDF, 210KB), pricing_breakdown_brightcart.xlsx (Excel, 45KB)

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
